title: Best Book Editors (2026): How to Hire One for Your Book
description: How to hire a book editor: which type of editing your manuscript needs, what to send, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: A book editor helps turn a manuscript into a book readers can enjoy from the first page to the last. There are different kinds of book editing, from big-picture story work to line-by-line polish. Authors are disappointed when they order the wrong type, skip a sample edit, or hire an editor who does not know their genre. This guide helps you choose the right edit.

faq.q: What types of book editing are there?
faq.a: Developmental editing looks at story, structure and characters. Line editing improves style and flow sentence by sentence. Copy editing fixes grammar, consistency and facts. Proofreading catches final errors before publication.

faq.q: Which edit do I need first?
faq.a: Usually developmental first, then line or copy editing, then proofreading. Polishing sentences in chapters you may later cut wastes money.

faq.q: Should I ask for a sample edit?
faq.a: Yes. A few pages edited by the editor show their style and whether they understand your book. Many offer this for a small fee.

faq.q: Does the editor need to know my genre?
faq.a: It helps a lot. Genres have conventions and reader expectations. Ask for books they have edited in your genre.
Usually with tracked changes and comments in Word, so you can accept or reject each edit.
